test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Kalpana and Sudha got 696 and 584 marks, respectively, in the same examination. If Kalpana scored 87% marks, then what is the percentage of marks scored by Sudha?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Comparison: 87% marks = 696 marks

Required % for Sudha = (87 ÷ 696) × 584

Required % = 0.125 × 584 = 73%

**∴ The correct answer is 73%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks obtained by **Kalpana** = 696

Percentage obtained by **Kalpana** = 87%

Marks obtained by **Sudha** = 584

**Formula Used:**

Total Marks = (Obtained Marks ÷ Percentage) × 100

Percentage = (Obtained Marks ÷ Total Marks) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb723e0aac7f962d36c43682b496d30b22672b67bc5e7e10c9b0966594b2126d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total marks be T.

⇒ 87% of T = 696

⇒ T = (696 × 100) ÷ 87

⇒ T = 8 × 100 = 800

⇒ Sudha's Percentage = (584 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Sudha's Percentage = 584 ÷ 8 = 73%

**∴ The correct answer is 73%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (New value − Old value) ÷ Old value × 100.

Base Change Property

If A is x% more than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100% less than A.

Unitary Method in Percentages

If x% corresponds to a value V, then 1% corresponds to V/x and 100% corresponds to (V/x) × 100.</p
